taxonomyNote: NatureServe places Nerodia in Colubridae; Illinois DNR lists the species under Natricidae. NatureServe notes N. floridana (Florida green watersnake) was formerly included in N. cyclopion.
fieldMarks: Medium-sized, heavy-bodied, dark semiaquatic snake, averaging 30-45 in.
Back greenish brown with obscure olive-brown or dark markings and dim black crossbars; belly dark grey or brown with yellow half-moon markings.
A short row of small subocular scales between the eye and the upper-lip scales separates it from other Missouri watersnakes.
Keeled scales; females larger than males.
behavior: Basks on logs, brush and banks, seldom far from water; flattens body and releases foul musk when disturbed.
Primarily diurnal in Illinois, almost exclusively nocturnal in Texas; hunts late evening.
Eats fish, frogs, salamanders, tadpoles, small turtles and invertebrates; live-bearing, young born August-September.
habitat: Cypress swamps, river sloughs, marshes, bayous, ditches, shallow lakes, oxbows and tree-lined sluggish streams, sometimes brackish Gulf Coast marshes.
range: Coastal Plain from extreme western Florida and southern Alabama to southeastern Texas and north in the Mississippi Valley to southeastern Missouri and southern Illinois.

lookalikes.name: Northern cottonmouth
lookalikes.howToTell: Cottonmouth is heavier-bodied with a chunky head, a facial pit between nostril and eye, and a light line from eye to mouth corner.
